title: Enterprise AI System Architecture & Harness Engineering
subtitle: Architect LLM-based and agentic systems, master harness engineering, orchestration topologies, and framework selection.

lessons.title: The AI System Landscape
lessons.hook: Enterprise leaders often label every AI initiative as 'agentic'. But if a task simply requires reading an invoice and returning a JSON summary, does an agentic loop add value, or does it merely introduce latency, cost, and unpredictable failure modes?
lessons.bigIdea: Enterprise AI is divided into LLM-based non-agentic systems and Agentic systems; for agentic systems, reliability is dictated not by the raw reasoning model, but by the harness engineering surrounding it.
lessons.plainEnglish: A Formula 1 engine (the reasoning model) produces raw horsepower. But without a carbon-fiber chassis, hydraulic brakes, telemetry sensors, and a roll cage (the harness), the car will crash into the first wall it encounters.
objectives: Distinguish LLM-based non-agentic systems from dynamic multi-step agentic systems
Deconstruct agentic systems into the Reasoning Model and Harness Engineering
Analyze why production failures overwhelmingly originate in the harness rather than the model
Map the 7 functional harness components required for dependable enterprise deployment

sections.title: Two Categories of AI Systems
sections.content:
AI systems are bifurcated by their runtime operational behavior:

1. LLM-Based Non-Agentic Systems: Input passes through a model to produce an output in a fixed, deterministic sequence. The system takes no autonomous runtime actions based on mid-process observations. Ideal for classification, extraction, and single-turn QA.

2. Agentic Systems: The system perceives an environment, reasons toward a goal, executes actions via tools, observes results, and dynamically chooses its next step. The execution trajectory is non-deterministic and expands across multi-turn loops.

sections.title: Reasoning Model vs. Harness Engineering
sections.content:
Every agentic system consists of two structural layers:

• The Reasoning Model: The core LLM (e.g. GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) that perceives current task state, plans sub-goals, and emits tool calls.
• Harness Engineering: The operational substrate surrounding the model. The harness provisions tools, manages working memory, compresses context, enforces security guardrails, and records telemetry.

Key Production Truth: Two systems powered by the exact same frontier model will exhibit wildly divergent production reliability depending on their harness. Models generate plausible next steps; harnesses make those steps safe, observable, and resilient.

sections.title: The 7 Core Harness Components
sections.content: A production-grade harness implements seven modular services:

tableData.Purpose: Functions connecting the model to APIs, databases, sandboxes, and file systems.
Selective retrieval, step summarization, and running state to prevent overflow.
Scope constraints, permission boundaries, token ceilings, and output regex filters.
Correlated execution tracing capturing every step, argument, latency, and token cost.
Self-reflection or critic models evaluating outputs before user delivery.
Multi-agent coordination (sequential, parallel, loop, hierarchical, handoff).

quiz.question: What is the defining runtime characteristic of an agentic system compared to a non-agentic LLM system?
options: Agentic systems use Python, whereas non-agentic systems use SQL
Agentic systems operate in an autonomous multi-step loop where the system selects its next action based on observations of previous tool outputs, rather than following a fixed processing path
Agentic systems always cost less per query
Agentic systems do not require prompts
quiz.correctAnswer: Agentic systems operate in an autonomous multi-step loop where the system selects its next action based on observations of previous tool outputs, rather than following a fixed processing path
quiz.explanation: Agency is defined by autonomous multi-step operation: perceiving state, selecting actions dynamically based on environmental observations, and iterating toward a goal.

quiz.question: Why do the majority of enterprise agentic failures originate in the harness rather than the reasoning model?
options: Because modern reasoning models are completely flawless
Because failures typically stem from unhandled tool exceptions, context window truncation, missing guardrails, stale memory, or unobservable execution paths
Because cloud providers do not monitor models
Because harnesses are written by external customers
quiz.correctAnswer: Because failures typically stem from unhandled tool exceptions, context window truncation, missing guardrails, stale memory, or unobservable execution paths
quiz.explanation: Frontier models can reason well, but if the harness feeds them truncated context, fails to catch a broken API return, or lacks guardrails against infinite loops, the system inevitably breaks in production.

recap: Distinguish LLM-based systems (fixed pipeline) from agentic systems (dynamic perception-action loop).
Agentic systems comprise two halves: the Reasoning Model and the Harness Engineering.
Production reliability is governed primarily by the quality and robustness of the harness.
Master the 7 harness components: Tools, Memory, Context Management, Guardrails, Observability, AI Review, and Orchestration.

lessons.title: LLM-Based Systems
lessons.hook: A client asks for an agent to route incoming customer support emails. You could build a complex 3-agent swarm, or you could write a single structured LLM call with a JSON schema. Which system ships in 3 days, costs 95% less, and never crashes?
lessons.bigIdea: LLM-based non-agentic systems form the high-ROI backbone of enterprise AI, excelling in classification, extraction, summarization, and RAG without the operational overhead of multi-step loops.
lessons.plainEnglish: A high-speed precision stamping press stamps out thousands of identical automotive brackets every hour. You don't need a walking humanoid robot with fingers to press a bracket when a purpose-built stamping tool does the job perfectly in a fraction of a second.
objectives: Master the 4 enterprise patterns: Classification, Extraction, Summarization, and QA
Architect production RAG systems across chunking, data freshness, context fit, and pipeline ownership
Evaluate Fine-Tuning tradeoffs: Full fine-tuning vs. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA)
Identify the 5 signals indicating an LLM-based system is the optimal architecture over an agent

sections.title: The 4 Core Patterns of LLM-Based Systems
sections.content:
Most enterprise workloads map directly to four foundational patterns:

1. Classification: Maps unstructured text to predefined categorical tags (e.g. support ticket routing, compliance triage). Evaluated via precision/recall against labeled test sets.
2. Extraction: Converts unstructured text into structured JSON schemas (e.g. invoice dates, counterparties, clause limits). Evaluated via schema conformance and field-level F1 scores.
3. Summarization & Synthesis: Compresses multi-page documents into structured executive briefs. Evaluated via factual consistency and coverage metrics.
4. Question Answering: Natural language answers grounded in curated enterprise source material.

sections.title: RAG-Based Knowledge Systems
sections.content:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) indices enterprise document stores into vector embeddings, dynamically retrieving semantically relevant chunks at query time.

4 Scoping & Evaluation Checkpoints for FDEs:
• Chunking Strategy: Splitting by paragraph or recursive character boundaries to avoid separating critical context.
• Data Freshness: Scheduled re-indexing workflows to prevent serving stale policies.
• Context Window Fit: Sizing top-k chunks so the prompt remains well beneath model context ceilings.
• Ingestion Pipeline Ownership: Defining who owns OCR preprocessing, document additions, and index re-computation post-handoff.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning: Full vs. PEFT (LoRA & QLoRA)
sections.content:
Fine-tuning updates model weights on domain-specific datasets when base models cannot reliably produce specialized output formats through prompt engineering alone.

• Full Fine-Tuning: Modifies all model parameters; highly compute-intensive, requiring high GPU memory and large labeled datasets.
• PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning): Updates a tiny fraction of parameters. Dominant technique: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), freezing base weights and training low-rank adapter matrices. QLoRA quantizes the base model to 4-bit, enabling fine-tuning on accessible commodity GPUs.

sections.title: When to Recommend an LLM-Based System
sections.content:
Always start with the simplest architecture that solves the problem. 5 signals to recommend an LLM-based system:

1. The task completes in a single or predictable sequence of model calls with zero mid-process tool exploration.
2. Input and output schemas are consistent and well-defined.
3. No external system state modifications or write-backs are required.
4. Low latency (sub-second) and strict token budget constraints are paramount.
5. The customer's operating team needs a system they can debug without managing session state or loop convergence.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational advantage of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) compared to full model fine-tuning?
options: It completely eliminates the need for training data
It freezes the base model weights and trains only small low-rank adapter matrices, drastically reducing GPU compute and memory requirements while preserving model quality
It converts Python code into C++
It prevents the model from ever generating numbers
quiz.correctAnswer: It freezes the base model weights and trains only small low-rank adapter matrices, drastically reducing GPU compute and memory requirements while preserving model quality
quiz.explanation: LoRA updates less than 1% of the model parameters via low-rank decomposition matrices, making fine-tuning vastly faster, cheaper, and deployable on commodity hardware.

quiz.question: Which of the following scenarios strongly warrants an LLM-based system over an agentic workflow?
options: A system that must autonomously research live financial news, formulate investment theses, and trade stocks via API
An enterprise pipeline that parses incoming vendor invoice PDFs, extracts 6 specific financial fields, and outputs a validated JSON payload for accounting
A web-browsing bot that clicks buttons and logs into multiple client portals to retrieve tax documents
A multi-agent team where a coder and tester debate unit test coverage
quiz.correctAnswer: An enterprise pipeline that parses incoming vendor invoice PDFs, extracts 6 specific financial fields, and outputs a validated JSON payload for accounting
quiz.explanation: Structured data extraction from consistent documents is a classic single-step LLM task. Introducing an agentic loop here introduces unnecessary latency, expense, and potential loop failure modes.

recap: LLM-based systems deliver immense enterprise value across Classification, Extraction, Summarization, and QA.
Production RAG requires rigorous chunking, freshness pipelines, context budgeting, and clear ingestion ownership.
PEFT techniques like LoRA and QLoRA provide cost-effective domain adaptation without full model re-training.
Default to LLM-based systems when tasks can be completed in a single step with constrained schemas.

lessons.title: Harness Engineering: Tools, Memory, and Context
lessons.hook: Your agent runs smoothly during a 3-step test. But when handling a complex 25-step enterprise workflow, the context window fills up, earlier instructions are silently dropped, and the agent hallucinates wildly. How do you engineer the harness to survive long-horizon execution?
lessons.bigIdea: Harness engineering turns a raw reasoning model into a stable runtime by orchestrating the 4-phase reasoning loop, governing tool risks, structuring dual-tier memory, and actively managing context windows.
lessons.plainEnglish: A pilot flying an airliner doesn't keep the entire 500-page flight manual in their lap. They keep a clean 1-page pre-flight checklist on the yoke, look up specific emergency procedures in the flight binder only when warning lights flash, and let the cockpit flight computer track fuel reserves in real time.
objectives: Master the 4-phase reasoning loop: Perceive → Reason → Act → Observe
Classify tools across Read, Write, and Execution risk profiles and enforce minimal access
Architect Short-Term (in-session working memory) vs. Long-Term (vector & relational) memory systems
Implement context compaction techniques: Step Summarization, Selective Retrieval, and Running State

sections.title: The 4-Phase Reasoning Loop
sections.content:
Every agentic system operates in a recurring execution cycle:

1. Perceive: The agent ingests current task state, prior tool results, and environmental signals.
2. Reason: The LLM processes accumulated context, deduces the immediate objective, and emits an action or tool call.
3. Act: The harness intercepts and executes the function against external services or databases.
4. Observe: The harness captures the tool's return payload and injects it as new perception for the next turn.

The loop repeats until a stopping condition is met, the goal is achieved, or a max-iteration guardrail trips.

sections.title: Tools & Enterprise Risk Profiles
sections.content:
Tools give the reasoning model physical agency. FDEs classify tools into three operational risk tiers:

• Read Tools: Fetch data from vector stores, databases, or public APIs. Zero state modification; lowest risk.
• Write Tools: Update CRM records, post Slack notifications, or submit database rows. Errors alter enterprise state and require audit logs and undo capabilities.
• Execution Tools: Run shell commands, execute Python scripts, or trigger cloud container spin-ups. Highest risk; requires isolated sandboxing (e.g. gVisor, Docker) and strict capability dropping.

sections.title: Dual-Tier Memory: Short-Term vs. Long-Term
sections.content:
Agents require two complementary memory systems:

• Short-Term Memory: Active in-session working memory held inside the LLM context window. High accessibility, zero retrieval latency, but strictly bounded by token capacity.
• Long-Term Memory: Durable external storage (vector databases for semantic similarity; relational databases for exact user IDs and records). Enables cross-session recall and episodic learning without retraining.

sections.title: Context Management & Silent Truncation Defense
sections.content:
Context window overflow is among the most pernicious enterprise failure modes: when token limits are reached, models silently drop earlier instructions or tool returns, generating plausible-sounding but catastrophic errors.

Three Context Compaction Strategies:
1. Step Summarization: Compacting earlier reasoning turns into dense summaries before context limits approach.
2. Selective Retrieval: Keeping large tool outputs in external storage and pulling only targeted snippets into the prompt.
3. Running State: Maintaining a lightweight, structured JSON whiteboard of verified facts that updates at each step, replacing the need to carry verbatim message histories.

quiz.question: Which category of agent tools carries the highest enterprise risk and requires sandboxed containment?
options: Read-only tools that query vector databases
Execution tools that run shell commands, execute Python scripts, or initiate container processes
Output formatting tools that convert markdown to HTML
Calculators that perform floating-point arithmetic
quiz.correctAnswer: Execution tools that run shell commands, execute Python scripts, or initiate container processes
quiz.explanation: Execution tools can modify host file systems, open network sockets, or consume arbitrary compute, demanding strict container isolation (e.g., non-root Docker or gVisor).

quiz.question: What happens during 'silent context window overflow' in an unmanaged agentic harness?
options: The computer automatically reboots
Earlier system prompts, instructions, or tool results are silently dropped from the context window, causing the model to hallucinate or violate constraints without throwing an explicit software error
The model stops speaking English
The database drops all tables
quiz.correctAnswer: Earlier system prompts, instructions, or tool results are silently dropped from the context window, causing the model to hallucinate or violate constraints without throwing an explicit software error
quiz.explanation: Without proactive context management, context truncation occurs silently. The LLM continues reasoning, but because foundational instructions or earlier facts are truncated, it makes disastrously erroneous decisions.

recap: The 4-phase reasoning loop (Perceive, Reason, Act, Observe) drives agentic execution.
Classify tools across Read, Write, and Execution profiles, applying sandboxing to high-risk tools.
Balance Short-Term working memory with Long-Term persistent memory to handle complex workflows.
Prevent silent context window overflow using Step Summarization, Selective Retrieval, and Running State whiteboards.

lessons.title: Harness Engineering: Guardrails, Observability, and Review
lessons.hook: An enterprise financial agent encounters an edge case, enters an infinite retry loop, makes 14,000 tool calls, and incurs a $38,000 API bill over the weekend. What critical harness components were missing?
lessons.bigIdea: Production readiness requires bounding agent behavior with multi-layer guardrails, instrumenting granular execution observability, inserting automated AI review loops, and designing calibrated human escalation workflows.
lessons.plainEnglish: A self-driving car doesn't just have a steering wheel and throttle. It has mechanical governor limits preventing it from exceeding 120 mph, an immutable black-box flight recorder logging every radar blip, a collision detection subsystem, and a steering wheel sensor that immediately alerts the human driver when lane markings disappear.
objectives: Configure the 4 enterprise guardrail types: Scope limits, Budget ceilings, Output filters, and Permission controls
Instrument execution observability across the 6 vital telemetry dimensions
Deploy AI review loops using self-reflection and independent critic models with retry limits
Design production human escalation workflows with calibrated confidence thresholds

sections.title: The 4 Enterprise Guardrail Types
sections.content:
Guardrails establish the immutable operating envelope of an agent:

1. Scope Limits: Whitelisting exact tools and API endpoints the agent may call. Prevents research agents from calling transactional endpoints.
2. Budget Ceilings: Hard caps on max tokens, max iteration turns (e.g. max 10 steps), and daily spend limits.
3. Output Filters: Regex scanners and validation models that strip PII, enforce JSON schema conformance, and block toxic or off-topic outputs.
4. Permission Controls: Enforcing role-based access control (RBAC) so agents only query records the active user is authorized to view.

sections.title: Observability & Tracing: The 6 Dimensions
sections.content:
When a multi-step agent fails, the bug almost never occurs at the final step—it occurred 5 steps earlier when a tool returned malformed JSON. An observable harness records 6 telemetry dimensions:

1. Tool invocations, arguments, return payloads, and execution latencies.
2. Exact prompt inputs and raw LLM completions at each turn.
3. Memory reads, writes, and retrieval similarity scores.
4. Token burn and financial cost per step and per session.
5. Error codes, network timeouts, and retry attempts.
6. Internal confidence scores and self-reflection critiques.

sections.title: AI Review Loops: Self-Reflection vs. Critic Models
sections.content:
Insert an automated evaluation step between generation and user delivery:

• Self-Reflection: Prompting the reasoning agent to critique its own output against factual grounding, completeness, and formatting rules.
• Critic Model: An independent, specialized model instance evaluating the output objectively without being influenced by the primary agent's reasoning trace.

Retry Limits: Always enforce a hard ceiling (e.g. maximum 2 regeneration retries). If the output fails after 2 retries, immediately route to human escalation.

sections.title: Calibrated Human Escalation
sections.content:
A production escalation workflow must define four operational elements:

1. The Trigger: Calibrated confidence scores (e.g. confidence < 0.88), flagged compliance categories, or exceeded retry limits.
2. What Accompanies It: The full execution trace, original user prompt, and specific reason for failure.
3. The Review Queue: A designated ticketing queue with assigned human reviewers and clear SLA turnaround times.
4. Pausing Behavior: The agent gracefully informs the user that their request is under expert review rather than hanging or failing silently.

quiz.question: What is the primary architectural difference between an AI review loop using 'Self-Reflection' versus an 'Independent Critic Model'?
options: Self-reflection requires C++ code, while a critic model uses Python

Self-reflection prompts the primary model to critique its own output, whereas a critic model uses a separate model instance that evaluates the output objectively without cognitive bias from the generation trace
Critic models are only used in video game development
Self-reflection is forbidden in enterprise deployments
quiz.correctAnswer: Self-reflection prompts the primary model to critique its own output, whereas a critic model uses a separate model instance that evaluates the output objectively without cognitive bias from the generation trace
quiz.explanation: A separate critic model avoids the blind spots of the generator agent, providing an objective second opinion on factual consistency and constraint compliance.

quiz.question: Why is execution tracing across all intermediate tool calls considered mandatory before an FDE hands off an agentic system?
options: Because cloud providers charge penalty fees if logs are missing
Because agentic failures are probabilistic and often originate several steps before the symptom surfaces; without correlated execution traces, customer engineers cannot reconstruct or debug failures
Because tracing makes LLMs generate text 10x faster
To prove that the model never made an API call
quiz.correctAnswer: Because agentic failures are probabilistic and often originate several steps before the symptom surfaces; without correlated execution traces, customer engineers cannot reconstruct or debug failures
quiz.explanation: In multi-step systems, an incorrect final output is often caused by an unhandled edge case in an earlier tool call. Without execution traces, debugging is impossible.

recap: Enforce the 4 enterprise guardrails: Scope limits, Budget ceilings, Output filters, and Permission controls.
Instrument telemetry across the 6 dimensions: tools, prompts, memory, token spend, errors, and confidence.
Implement AI review loops with strict retry limits to catch hallucinations before delivery.
Design calibrated human escalation paths with designated review queues and transparent context packages.

lessons.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Patterns
lessons.hook: When should you graduate from a single agent with multiple tools to a multi-agent system? If you divide a simple task among 4 agents, you might quadruple token costs and latency while creating new points of coordination failure. When is multi-agent actually justified?
lessons.bigIdea: Multi-agent systems distribute work across specialized agents when task parallelism, distinct tool sets, or context boundaries exceed single-agent capacity; choosing the right orchestration topology determines production viability.
lessons.plainEnglish: A single master chef can run a small café kitchen efficiently. But in a 500-seat banquet kitchen, you need specialized stations: a pastry chef, a saucier, a butcher, and an executive chef coordinating tickets so dishes arrive hot and synchronized.
objectives: Evaluate the 3 conditions that genuinely justify a multi-agent architecture
Master the 4 core orchestration patterns: Sequential, Parallel, Loop, and Hierarchical
Implement Agent Handoffs with rigorous context payload validation
Mitigate the 4 multi-agent production hazards: State drift, cascading failures, unobservable boundaries, and cost multiplication

sections.title: When Multi-Agent is the Right Choice
sections.content:
Single-agent systems with well-engineered harnesses are faster, cheaper, and easier to debug. Multi-agent is justified ONLY when:

1. Sub-tasks can execute independently in parallel, meaningfully compressing wall-clock turnaround time.
2. Different sub-tasks demand genuinely distinct tool sets or security scopes that a single agent cannot safely carry.
3. The total context required exceeds the reliable context window capacity of a single agent.

sections.title: The 4 Core Orchestration Topologies
sections.content:
Enterprise multi-agent architectures draw upon four structural patterns:

• Sequential Orchestration: A linear pipeline where Agent A processes input, hands its output to Agent B, which hands off to Agent C. Highly predictable and straightforward to debug.
• Parallel Orchestration: Multiple agents execute simultaneously across independent sub-tasks (e.g. analyzing 5 documents at once). Output is aggregated into a synthesized result.
• Loop Orchestration: Agents run in an iterative refinement cycle (e.g. Coder Agent → Evaluator Agent → Revision) until an exit threshold or max-turns limit is met.
• Hierarchical Orchestration: A central Orchestrator Agent plans the macro strategy, delegates specialized sub-tasks to Worker Agents, and synthesizes intermediate findings. Workers do not talk to each other.

sections.title: Agent Handoff & Context Validation
sections.content:
In an Agent Handoff, Agent A transfers active execution control to Agent B and then terminates. There is no central manager continually arbitrating turns.

Context Validation Requirement: When Agent A hands off, it must pass a validated, structured context payload (task goal, verified facts, constraints). If the handoff payload is malformed, Agent B fails immediately—a failure originating in Agent A that surfaces in Agent B. Rigorous schema validation at handoff boundaries is non-negotiable.

sections.title: Multi-Agent Coordination Hazards
sections.content:
Four hazards must be engineered against before production rollout:

• State Drift: Context becoming corrupted or contradictory as it passes through multiple agent turns.
• Failure Cascades: An unhandled exception in one worker agent halting the entire pipeline. (Mitigation: isolated worker timeouts and fallback defaults).
• Multi-Agent Observability: Ensuring traces are linked with a global session ID across all agent hops.
• Cost & Latency Multiplication: Parallel and loop topologies multiply token spend exponentially; FDEs must calculate per-task costs at full volume during scoping.

quiz.question: What is the primary failure mode of unvalidated 'Agent Handoffs' in multi-agent pipelines?
options: The model runs out of hard drive space
Agent A passes an incomplete, ambiguous, or malformed context payload to Agent B, causing Agent B to fail or hallucinate even though the bug originated in Agent A
The Python compiler throws a syntax error
The network cable disconnects
quiz.correctAnswer: Agent A passes an incomplete, ambiguous, or malformed context payload to Agent B, causing Agent B to fail or hallucinate even though the bug originated in Agent A
quiz.explanation: Without schema-validated handoff payloads, errors in upstream agents propagate silently into downstream agents, making root-cause diagnosis exceptionally difficult.

quiz.question: In which scenario is 'Parallel Orchestration' the most effective multi-agent pattern?
options: When each step depends strictly on the output of the preceding step
When analyzing 10 independent contracts simultaneously, where each contract can be processed in isolation and results aggregated at the end
When an agent is debugging code in an iterative trial-and-error loop
When a user is having a single-turn conversational greeting
quiz.correctAnswer: When analyzing 10 independent contracts simultaneously, where each contract can be processed in isolation and results aggregated at the end
quiz.explanation: Parallel orchestration is ideal for decomposing embarrassingly parallel, independent tasks, drastically reducing overall latency by running simultaneous worker agents.

recap: Graduate to multi-agent architectures only when task parallelism, tool specialization, or context limits justify the coordination cost.
Select from 4 orchestration topologies: Sequential, Parallel, Loop, and Hierarchical.
Enforce strict schema validation on context payloads at Agent Handoff boundaries.
Defend against state drift, cascading failures, unobservable hops, and exponential token multiplication.

lessons.title: Choosing an Agentic Framework
lessons.hook: LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK... With so many frameworks competing for mindshare, how does an FDE choose the right tool for an enterprise deployment that customer engineers can maintain long after handoff?
lessons.bigIdea: Framework selection is an early architectural decision evaluated across 5 pragmatic criteria: Design philosophy fit, Model affinity, Built-in observability, Implementation speed, and Post-handoff ownership.
lessons.plainEnglish: Choosing a framework is like picking a chassis for a delivery fleet. If the customer's mechanics only know how to service diesel trucks, building a fleet of exotic hydrogen vehicles will leave them stranded the first time an engine warning light flashes.
objectives: Differentiate framework scaffolding from fundamental architectural design decisions
Compare major enterprise frameworks: LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and Vendor SDKs
Apply the 5 Selection Criteria when recommending a framework from scratch
Navigate customer environments where an agentic framework has already been chosen

sections.title: What Frameworks Provide vs. Design Decisions
sections.content:
Frameworks supply the plumbing: state management primitives, tool binding syntax, memory connectors, and tracing hooks. They significantly compress implementation time and provide battle-tested abstractions.

However, frameworks do NOT make architectural design decisions. The FDE still determines which orchestration pattern fits, how guardrails are calibrated, what handoff schemas look like, and how observability is structured. A framework accelerates implementation—it does not substitute for sound system design.

sections.title: The Modern Framework Landscape
sections.content: Enterprise agentic development centers around several major frameworks:

tableData.Best For: Broadest tool ecosystem; RAG workflows and sequential tool calling.
Complex cyclical loops, conditional branching, and explicit persistent state machines.
Human organizational metaphor (researcher, writer, editor) for business process automation.
Multi-agent debate, code verification, and back-and-forth critique loops.
Tight native integration with GPT models and function calling.
Native Google Cloud deployments, Vertex AI, and Gemini reasoning models.

sections.title: The 5 Framework Selection Criteria
sections.content:
When recommending a framework from scratch, evaluate across five dimensions:

1. Design Philosophy Fit: Match the framework's abstraction (graphs, roles, conversations) to how the team naturally thinks about the problem.
2. Model Affinity & Flexibility: Vendor SDKs provide tight integration with their models; open-source frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI) prevent vendor lock-in.
3. Built-In Observability: Frameworks with native OpenTelemetry or tracing support (e.g. LangSmith, Phoenix) eliminate building custom telemetry.
4. Implementation Velocity: Weighing the learning curve against sprint deadlines (e.g. 2-week POC vs. 6-month enterprise build).
5. Post-Handoff Ownership: If the customer's engineering team cannot independently debug the framework after handoff, it is the WRONG framework.

sections.title: When the Customer Has Already Chosen
sections.content:
In most field engagements, the customer's team already has a framework in place. Three scenarios:

• It Fits: Adopt it enthusiastically. Respect their existing conventions and accelerate build velocity.
• Suboptimal but Workable: Work within it. Document constraints and tradeoffs in the handoff document without forcing a disruptive rewrite.
• Genuinely Blocks Delivery: Recommend a switch framed around delivery risk and timeline impact. Present empirical evidence showing why the current framework cannot support required state or latency constraints.

quiz.question: Which framework is best suited for an enterprise workflow that requires complex cyclical loops, conditional branching, and persistent graph-based state machines?
options: LangGraph
A basic bash script
CrewAI role-based crews
A spreadsheet formula
quiz.explanation: LangGraph explicitly models workflows as directed graphs with nodes (actions) and edges (conditional transitions), providing fine-grained control over cyclical loops and persistent state.

quiz.question: What is the single most important criterion when an FDE selects an agentic framework for an enterprise customer?
options: Which framework has the most GitHub stars this week
Post-Handoff Ownership: Whether the customer's engineering team can confidently understand, debug, and maintain the system after the FDE leaves
Which framework uses the newest beta features
Which framework requires the longest code files
quiz.correctAnswer: Post-Handoff Ownership: Whether the customer's engineering team can confidently understand, debug, and maintain the system after the FDE leaves
quiz.explanation: If the customer team cannot maintain the framework after the FDE departs, the project will degrade into shelfware. Maintainability and team ownership are paramount.

recap: Frameworks supply plumbing and state primitives; FDEs make the architectural and guardrail decisions.
Compare LangGraph (graphs), CrewAI (roles), AutoGen (conversations), and Vendor SDKs (native integration).
Evaluate frameworks using the 5 Criteria: Philosophy fit, Model affinity, Observability, Speed, and Ownership.
Prioritize post-handoff maintainability: the best framework is the one the customer team can operate independently.
